import os
import json
import subprocess
import time
import requests
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP('repo-ci')
CI_WEBHOOK_URL = os.environ.get('CI_STATUS_WEBHOOK_URL', 'https://ci.internal.example.com/hooks/test-results')
CI_WEBHOOK_TOKEN = os.environ.get('CI_STATUS_WEBHOOK_TOKEN', '')
TEST_HISTORY_FILE = '.ci_test_history.jsonl'


def _append_test_history(repo_path: str, payload: dict) -> None:
    # Keep a local log of test runs so trends can be inspected without the CI server
    record = {k: payload[k] for k in ('commit', 'status', 'exit_code', 'duration_seconds')}
    record['recorded_at'] = time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', time.gmtime())
    with open(os.path.join(repo_path, TEST_HISTORY_FILE), 'a', encoding='utf-8') as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps(record) + '\n')


@mcp.tool()
def run_test_suite_and_post_results(repo_path: str, commit_sha: str, test_path: str='tests') -> dict:
    started = time.time()
    proc = subprocess.run(['python', '-m', 'pytest', test_path, '-q', '--maxfail=50'], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=1800)
    duration = round(time.time() - started, 2)
    output_tail = '\n'.join(proc.stdout.splitlines()[-40:])
    payload = {'commit': commit_sha, 'status': 'passed' if proc.returncode == 0 else 'failed', 'exit_code': proc.returncode, 'duration_seconds': duration, 'summary': output_tail}
    _append_test_history(repo_path, payload)
    resp = requests.post(CI_WEBHOOK_URL, json=payload, headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {CI_WEBHOOK_TOKEN}'}, timeout=15)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return {'status': payload['status'], 'exit_code': proc.returncode, 'duration_seconds': duration, 'webhook_status': resp.status_code}
